newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia court defers sentencing foreign journalist.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia court defers sentencing foreign journalist.

text.p: Malaysia's High Court on Monday delayed for seven weeks the sentencing of a foreign journalist found guilty of contempt of court, the national Bernama news agency reported.
Murray Hiebert, a journalist with the Far Eastern Economic Review, will know his penalty on September 4 for questioning a civil suit brought against a school by a judge's wife.

Chandra Sri Ram was suing the International School of Kuala Lumpur for dropping her son, Govind, from its debating team. Hiebert had written an article on the suit, published in the Review on January 23, while the case still was in progress.
The suit was settled on March 10 after the school agreed to apologise openly in court.
The 47-year-old Hiebert was found guilty of contempt of court on May 30 and was supposed to have been sentenced on Monday.
But Justice Low Hop Bing, who presided over the case, said on Monday he needed five weeks to write his judgement and set sentencing on September 4.
Chandra's lawyer Kam Woon Wah urged the court to impose a jail sentence on Hiebert, arguing that a lenient judgement would send the wrong signal to other reporters in Malaysia.
"That (Hiebert is a journalist) is not an excuse because if that is allowed, then the journalists can write articles of this nature everyday," said Kam.
Hiebert's lawyer, Muhammad Shafee Abdullah, pleaded for leniency, saying since his client was a foreigner, dealing with and writing about local laws was not an easy task.
Shafee also said that the Review, a weekly news magazine, has offered to correct the "errors" in Hiebert's article.
Justice Low, who had fixed bail at 100,000 ringgit ($39,525), allowed Hiebert to retrieve his passport, held earlier by the court.
Chandra had said in her suit against Hiebert that his article in the Review, entitled "See You in Court", amounted to an attack on the Malaysian judiciary.
The suit referred to a passage in the article, in which Hiebert noted that Govind was the son of Court of Appeals Judge Gopal Sri Ram and the case appeared to have sped through Malaysia's judiciary.
